title: RFQ Course Failure Categories
description: Controlled vocabulary for scenario_responses.selected_failure_category. Single source of truth for all failure classification dropdowns in the course application.

categories.label: No single source of truth
categories.description: Multiple conflicting versions of the same data exist across systems, teams, or documents. No authoritative record is designated.
categories.example: A customer receives a quote, a verbal price, and an invoice that don't match.

categories.label: Intake / minimum viable complete record failure
categories.description: The data collected at entry is incomplete, ambiguous, or unvalidated — causing downstream misrouting, duplication, or processing failures.
categories.example: Free-text company names produce five variants of the same entity; the RFQ is misrouted.

categories.label: Dirty-state visibility missing
categories.description: Estimated, unconfirmed, or in-progress data is presented as final — or no mechanism exists to distinguish confirmed from estimated state.
categories.example: An estimated lead time is treated as confirmed; the order ships late.

categories.label: Vague commitments / declarations instead of proof
categories.description: Responses assert capability or status without specific dates, conditions, or verifiable evidence. Customer escalates due to unresolved ambiguity.
categories.example: A customer receives vague timelines in three consecutive replies.

categories.label: Vendor data / translation failure
categories.description: Vendor-supplied data uses different schemas, units, part numbers, or terminology that is not mapped to internal standards before use.
categories.example: A vendor's lead time convention differs from internal definitions; the mismatch is never resolved.

categories.label: Transparent substitution failure
categories.description: A product, component, or data substitution is made without disclosure to the affected party, causing downstream errors.
categories.example: A customer installs the wrong product because a substitution was never disclosed.

categories.label: Naming / governance confusion
categories.description: Inconsistent naming, ambiguous status labels, or absent governance rules cause data to be misread, misreported, or technically indebted.
categories.example: A status field labeled 'complete' is applied to orders that never shipped.
